Summary ModelSlim W8A8_DYNAMIC checkpoints of Qwen3.5 (GDN hybrid, e.g. Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8) load incorrectly on Ascend NPU: the fused linear-attention projections and the whole vision tower silently fall back to unquantized loading (int8 weights copied raw into bf16 params → garbage output, with only not found in params_dict warnings), and once quantized, the first vision-tower matmul crashes the server at warmup with an ACL parameter error. Three independent bugs are fixed: 1. Unresolved fused-GDN scheme — the model side fuses in_proj_qkv + in_proj_z into in_proj_qkvz (and in_proj_b + in_proj_a into in_proj_ba) while the ModelSlim checkpoint records the unfused per-projection names. ModelSlimConfig._quant_prefix_candidates() now maps the fused names onto their shards, so in_proj_qkvz resolves to W8A8_DYNAMIC instead of falling through to UnquantizedLinearMethod (48 layers × missing weight_scale/weight_offset). 2. Vision encoder forced unquantized — Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration hardcoded quant_config=None for Qwen3VLMoeVisionModel, but ModelSlim checkpoints quantize the vision tower (attn.qkv/attn.proj/mlp.linear_fc1 are W8A8_DYNAMIC). The config is now forwarded when isinstance(quant_config, ModelSlimConfig) (same gating as kimi_vl_moonvit.py); GPTQ/AWQ/BitsAndBytes paths keep quant_config=None exactly as before. 3. NPU W8A8 kernels reject 3-D input — the vision tower feeds linears (seq, 1, hidden) activations (x.unsqueeze(1) in Qwen3VLMoeVisionModel.forward); the bf16 path broadcasts fine but npu_dynamic_quant/npu_quantize/npu_quant_matmul only accept 2-D (ACL error 161002). Both NPUW8A8Int8LinearMethod and NPUW8A8Int8DynamicLinearMethod.apply now flatten leading batch dims into m for the NPU ops and restore the layout afterwards. 2-D inputs (all language-model layers) are byte-identical. Changes python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py _quant_prefix_candidates(): add fused-GDN candidates (in_proj_qkvz → in_proj_qkv/in_proj_z, in_proj_ba → in_proj_b/in_proj_a) and model.visual. ↔ visual. prefix variants. python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py Forward quant_config to Qwen3VLMoeVisionModel when it is a ModelSlimConfig. python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/linear_method_npu.py Flatten 3-D inputs to 2-D in both W8A8 apply() methods and restore shape on output. Total: +54 / −13 lines across 3 files. Functional verification Real TP=1 server run on Ascend NPU with Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 (--quantization modelslim): - 0 Unsupported Linear modelslim scheme warnings (was 48), 0 not found in params_dict (was 208+) - Server starts and passes warmup (quantized vision-tower forward) - Text generation correct (1+1=? → 2); multimodal request correctly describes the test image (objects and colors) - Radix cache hits observed
Accuracy bf16 w8a8
Performance (性能测试) bf16 w8a8
Scope Only the modelslim quantization path changes behavior; 2-D linear paths (all language-model layers) are byte-identical. The kernel change also benefits compressed-tensors W8A8 int8 on NPU, which shares NPUW8A8Int8DynamicLinearMethod. Other quantization methods (GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/MXFP4/bnb) are untouched. Fixes #36423 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #35826070880](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35826070880) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35826070683](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35826070683) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35826070865](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35826070865)

nodes.body:
Regarding the first bug described in this PR, **“Unresolved fused-GDN scheme”**, thanks for identifying and fixing the issue. I added temporary debug logging around `packed_modules_mapping` and the ModelSlim quantization lookup to provide some additional runtime information.

For the Qwen3.8-27B-W8A8 checkpoint on NPU, the raw mapping received by ModelSlim currently has the following mixed structure:

```jsonc
{
  // From Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping
  "qkv_proj": [
    "q_proj",
    "k_proj",
    "v_proj"
  ],
  "gate_up_proj": [
    "gate_proj",
    "up_proj"
  ],
  "in_proj_qkvz": [
    "in_proj_qkv",
    "in_proj_z"
  ],
  "in_proj_ba": [
    "in_proj_b",
    "in_proj_a"
  ],

  // Appended to the same mapping by the NPU loader
  "visual": {
    "qkv_proj": [
      "qkv"
    ],
    "gate_up_proj": [
      "gate_proj",
      "up_proj"
    ]
  },
  "vision_model": {
    "qkv_proj": [
      "q_proj",
      "k_proj",
      "v_proj"
    ],
    "proj": [
      "out_proj"
    ]
  },
  "model": {
    "qkv_proj": [
      "q_proj",
      "k_proj",
      "v_proj"
    ],
    "gate_up_proj": [
      "gate_proj",
      "up_proj"
    ],
    "fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa": [
      "q_a_proj",
      "kv_a_proj_with_mqa"
    ],
    "index_qkv_proj": [
      "index_q_proj",
      "index_k_proj"
    ]
  }
}
```

This mapping is used by ModelSlim to resolve an SGLang runtime fused-module name to the corresponding checkpoint-side entry in `quant_model_description.json`. ModelSlim then uses the resolved checkpoint entry to select the quantization scheme, such as W8A8/INT8 or FLOAT.

The mixed mapping is constructed from two sources:

1. The Qwen3.5 model class declares a flat model-specific mapping, including:

   ```python
   "in_proj_qkvz": ["in_proj_qkv", "in_proj_z"],
   "in_proj_ba": ["in_proj_b", "in_proj_a"],
   ```

   Source: [`Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/cebbaacae45ebf669101dde3aac4817ecbb038e0/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L1303-L1311)

2. On NPU, the loader retrieves that model-class mapping and appends the nested `"model"`, `"visual"` and `"vision_model"` mappings.

   Source: [`_get_quantization_config()` NPU mapping injection](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/cebbaacae45ebf669101dde3aac4817ecbb038e0/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py#L218-L251)

The resulting object therefore mixes two different value types:

```text
Dict[str, List[str] | Dict[str, List[str]]]
```

while the original `packed_modules_mapping` contract is a flat:

```text
Dict[str, List[str]]
```

The current ModelSlim implementation selects only one nested subgroup:

```python
key = "model"
if "vision_model" in prefix:
    key = "vision_model"
elif "visual" in prefix:
    key = "visual"

packed_modules_mapping_subset = self.packed_modules_mapping.get(key, {})
```

Source: [`ModelSlimConfig.get_quant_method()`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/cebbaacae45ebf669101dde3aac4817ecbb038e0/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py#L266-L285)

For a language-model layer, this means ModelSlim uses only:

```json
{
  "qkv_proj": [
    "q_proj",
    "k_proj",
    "v_proj"
  ],
  "gate_up_proj": [
    "gate_proj",
    "up_proj"
  ],
  "fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa": [
    "q_a_proj",
    "kv_a_proj_with_mqa"
  ],
  "index_qkv_proj": [
    "index_q_proj",
    "index_k_proj"
  ]
}
```

The model-declared outer mappings for `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba` are still present in the raw object, but become invisible after the `"model"` subgroup is selected.

Consequently, ModelSlim cannot resolve:

```text
in_proj_qkvz -> in_proj_qkv / in_proj_z
in_proj_ba   -> in_proj_b / in_proj_a
```

before querying `quant_model_description.json`. This causes incorrect downstream handling of the W8A8 `in_proj_qkvz` projection and the floating-point `in_proj_ba` projection.

At least three potential fix directions appear possible:

1. Add `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba` to the NPU loader’s hard-coded `"model"` subgroup.
2. Add Qwen3.5 GDN fused-name aliases inside ModelSlim, as proposed in this PR.
3. Teach ModelSlim to understand the existing mixed mapping structure by retaining the model-declared outer flat mappings and applying the selected NPU subgroup as a scoped override.

I am providing this mainly as runtime debug information related to the first bug. The preferred fix likely needs discussion because these alternatives have different compatibility and maintenance trade-offs.

Regarding the second bug described in this PR, **“Vision encoder forced unquantized”**, I noticed a possible compatibility issue in the new prefix-handling logic in `_quant_prefix_candidates()`.

Previously, every candidate that did not start with `language_model.` would also get a `language_model.` version:

```python
if candidate.startswith("language_model."):
    candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("language_model."))
else:
    candidates.append(f"language_model.{candidate}")
```

The PR changes this to:

```python
if candidate.startswith("language_model."):
    candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("language_model."))
elif candidate.startswith("model.visual."):
    candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("model."))
elif candidate.startswith("visual."):
    candidates.append(f"model.{candidate}")
```

The new `model.visual.*` / `visual.*` handling is needed for the quantized vision encoder. However, changing the original `else` into `elif` also means that ordinary candidates no longer get the old `language_model.` fallback.

For example, for this input:

```text
model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
```

the old code generated these candidates:

```text
model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.down_proj
language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
language_model.model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.down_proj
```

With the code in this PR, only these candidates are generated:

```text
model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.down_proj
```

Therefore, these two candidates disappear:

```text
language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
language_model.model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.down_proj
```

The `language_model.` fallback was added for checkpoints whose quantization metadata keeps that outer prefix, so removing it may affect those checkpoints.

I confirmed the candidate-list difference through static code analysis, but I have not reproduced an actual runtime failure. Would it be safer to keep the language-model prefix handling and the vision prefix handling as two independent operations? For example:

```python
for candidate in list(candidates):
    if candidate.startswith("language_model."):
        candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("language_model."))
    else:
        candidates.append(f"language_model.{candidate}")

    if candidate.startswith("model.visual."):
        candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("model."))
    elif candidate.startswith("visual."):
        candidates.append(f"model.{candidate}")
```

This keeps the new vision-prefix support while preserving the previous `language_model.` fallback behavior.
@fishAndShrimp  These improvements are very helpful. I’ve merged your suggestions in the new version.

### GPQA-Diamond accuracy verification Following up on the accuracy test request, I evaluated this PR at commit [`8786461`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/8786461159ca3fe98c94369f6411ea31d6d75e24) with `Qwen3.8-27B-W8A8` on Ascend NPU using ModelSlim quantization. Test environment: - Hardware: Ascend 910 (`64 GiB` HBM per device), `TP=2` - NPU system-management tool: `npu-smi 25.5.1` - Software: CANN `9.0.0`, EvalScope `1.11.1` | Run | Samples | Accuracy | | --- | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 198 | 90.4% | | 2 | 198 | 90.4% | Both completed evaluations produced the same `90.4%` accuracy. For reference, the official [Qwen3.8-27B model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B#text-performance) reports a GPQA-Diamond score of `89.2`. Run 2 was interrupted after 192 predictions because the serving endpoint became unavailable. After restarting the server, I resumed from the EvalScope cache and completed the remaining 6 samples. The final result above includes all 198 samples.
Run 1 result
Run 2 result
Sanitized EvalScope command ```bash evalscope eval \ --model "/PATH/TO/Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8/" \ --api-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 \ --api-key EMPTY \ --eval-type openai_api \ --generation-config '{ "temperature": 0.9, "max_tokens": 260000, "seed": 3407, "n": 1, "timeout": 3600, "stream": true, "extra_body": { "chat_template_kwargs": { "enable_thinking": true } } }' \ --datasets gpqa_diamond \ --dataset-hub Local \ --dataset-args '{ "gpqa_diamond": { "local_path": "/PATH/TO/gpqa_diamond", "shuffle": true, "shuffle_choices": true } }' \ --eval-batch-size 32 \ --ignore-errors ``` The SGLang server was launched with `--device npu --attention-backend ascend --quantization modelslim --tp-size 2` and NEXTN speculative decoding (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens).

Serving Performance Benchmark Verification

Following up on the performance test request, I evaluated this PR at commit https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/8786461159ca3fe98c94369f6411ea31d6d75e24 with Qwen3.8‑27B on Ascend NPU. Two sets of benchmarks were executed: native bf16 precision and ModelSlim W8A8 quantized weight.

Test Environment

  • Hardware: Ascend 910 (64 GiB HBM per device), TP=2
  • NPU system‑management tool: npu‑smi 25.5.1
  • Software: CANN 9.0.0
  • Benchmark tool: sglang.bench_serving
  • Benchmark parameters:
python -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
    --backend sglang \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port 6688 \
    --gsp-num-groups 1 \
    --gsp-prompts-per-group 20 \
    --gsp-system-prompt-len 57600 \
    --gsp-question-len 6400 \
    --gsp-output-len 1000 \
    --max-concurrency 20 \
    --num-prompts 80 \
    --request-rate inf

Benchmark Summary

Traffic request rate: inf, Max request concurrency: 20, Total 80 successful requests for each run.

Metric | bf16 | W8A8 (ModelSlim)
-- | -- | --
Mean TTFT (ms) | 23970.37 | 19940.48
Mean TPOT (ms) | 45.83 | 41.45
Output token throughput (tok/s) | 275.78 | 312.96
bf16 full benchmark raw log (click to expand)
W8A8 (ModelSlim) full benchmark raw log (click to expand)

Observation

Compared with bf16 baseline, ModelSlim W8A8 quantization achieves better output token throughput, lower mean TTFT and mean TPOT under high‑concurrency long‑prompt scenario. All 80 requests completed successfully in both test runs. W8A8 also brings improvement on input token throughput and overall end‑to‑end latency, while P95/P99 latency still shows noticeable tail latency for long‑prompt workload.

### Also required for the `W8A8_MXFP8` path

Confirming this PR is needed beyond the int8 `W8A8_DYNAMIC` case in the issue. We hit the same failure with a ModelSlim **`W8A8_MXFP8`** checkpoint of Qwen3.5-27B on Ascend 950, served through the offline ModelSlim path (`--device npu --tp 1`, scheme auto-detected from `quant_model_description.json`).

**Before this PR**, every GDN layer lost its scheme and then its scales:

```
Unsupported Linear modelslim scheme: [''] in layer: model.language_model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_qkvz
Unsupported Linear modelslim scheme: [''] in layer: model.language_model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_ba
Parameter model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_qkvz.weight_scale not found in params_dict
```

repeated for every linear-attention layer, plus the vision tower (`visual.blocks.*.attn.qkv_proj`, `attn.proj`, `mlp.linear_fc1`, `mlp.linear_fc2`, `visual.merger.*`). The server started and answered, but the output was garbage.

**Why this is not int8-specific.** Three of the four changes here are naming/mapping fixes that run *before* scheme dispatch:

- `loader.py`: `in_proj_qkvz -> [in_proj_qkv, in_proj_z]`, `in_proj_ba -> [in_proj_b, in_proj_a]`
- `modelslim.py::get_quant_method`: redirect to the unfused component name the checkpoint actually stores
- `modelslim.py::_quant_prefix_candidates`: `model.visual.` <-> `visual.`

The lookup fails before `get_linear_scheme()` ever chooses between `ModelSlimW8A8Int8` and `ModelSlimMXFP8Scheme`, so the scheme string in the checkpoint is irrelevant: it returns `None`, the layer becomes `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, and the float8 weights are copied raw into bf16 parameters. Only the fourth change (folding 3-D vision inputs to 2-D in the W8A8 int8 kernels) is int8-specific; `NPUMXFP8LinearMethod` already reshapes to 2-D, so MXFP8 needs nothing there.

**After this PR**: no `Unsupported Linear modelslim scheme` warnings, no `not found in params_dict`, and generation is correct again.

**One caveat for MXFP8, separate from this PR.** Once the vision tower receives the ModelSlim config, `ModelSlimMXFP8Scheme.create_weights` sizes the weight-scale placeholder as `K // 32`, one column short for the vision MLP down projection. A ModelSlim `W8A8_MXFP8` export of Qwen3.5-27B stores it as:

```
model.visual.blocks.0.mlp.linear_fc2.weight        [1152, 4304]   W8A8_MXFP8
model.visual.blocks.0.mlp.linear_fc2.weight_scale  [1152,  135]   W8A8_MXFP8
```

`ceil(4304 / 32) = 135` while the placeholder allocates 134, so the parameter fails to load; 135 is also odd, which the `reshape(n, k // 2, 2)` pair layout in `process_weights_after_loading` cannot consume. Rounding up and padding the odd scale count is in sgl-project/sglang#32745. It is independent of this PR and does not block it -- the same block's `linear_fc1` has `K=1152` with 36 scales and is unaffected.

files.patch:
@@ -96,9 +96,11 @@ def apply(
         from sglang.srt.layers.linear import RowParallelLinear
 
         original_dtype = x.dtype
+        original_shape = x.shape
+        x_2d = x.reshape(-1, original_shape[-1]) if x.ndim > 2 else x
         if original_dtype != torch.int8:
-            x = torch.ops.npu.npu_quantize(
-                x,
+            x_2d = torch.ops.npu.npu_quantize(
+                x_2d,
                 layer.aclnn_input_scale_reciprocal,
                 layer.aclnn_input_offset,
                 torch.qint8,
@@ -111,13 +113,16 @@ def apply(
             quant_bias = None
         else:
             quant_bias = layer.quant_bias
-        return torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul(
-            x,
+        out = torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul(
+            x_2d,
             layer.weight,
             layer.deq_scale,
             bias=quant_bias,
             output_dtype=original_dtype,
         )
+        if x.ndim > 2:
+            out = out.reshape(*original_shape[:-1], -1)
+        return out
 
 
 class NPUW8A8Int8DynamicLinearMethod(_NPULinearMethodBase):
@@ -142,17 +147,33 @@ def apply(
             """dynamic_scale is calculated in malprolog kernel"""
             original_dtype = torch.bfloat16
             quant_out, dynamic_scale = x
-        else:
-            original_dtype = x.dtype
-            quant_out, dynamic_scale = torch.ops.npu.npu_dynamic_quant(x)
-        return torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul(
+            return torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul(
+                quant_out,
+                layer.weight,
+                layer.weight_scale,
+                pertoken_scale=dynamic_scale.flatten(),
+                bias=bias,
+                output_dtype=original_dtype,
+            )
+
+        # The vision encoder feeds linears a 3-D (seq, 1, hidden) layout that
+        # the NPU quant ops only accept flattened to 2-D.  Fold the leading
+        # batch dims into m for the quantized GEMM, then restore the layout.
+        original_dtype = x.dtype
+        original_shape = x.shape
+        x_2d = x.reshape(-1, original_shape[-1]) if x.ndim > 2 else x
+        quant_out, dynamic_scale = torch.ops.npu.npu_dynamic_quant(x_2d)
+        out = torch.ops.npu.npu_quant_matmul(
             quant_out,
             layer.weight,
             layer.weight_scale,
             pertoken_scale=dynamic_scale.flatten(),
             bias=bias,
             output_dtype=original_dtype,
         )
+        if x.ndim > 2:
+            out = out.reshape(*original_shape[:-1], -1)
+        return out
 
 
 class NPUMXFP8LinearMethod(_NPULinearMethodBase):

issue_comments.body:
Regarding the first bug described in this PR, **“Unresolved fused-GDN scheme”**, thanks for identifying and fixing the issue. I added temporary debug logging around `packed_modules_mapping` and the ModelSlim quantization lookup to provide some additional runtime information.

For the Qwen3.8-27B-W8A8 checkpoint on NPU, the raw mapping received by ModelSlim currently has the following mixed structure:

```jsonc
{
  // From Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping
  "qkv_proj": [
    "q_proj",
    "k_proj",
    "v_proj"
  ],
  "gate_up_proj": [
    "gate_proj",
    "up_proj"
  ],
  "in_proj_qkvz": [
    "in_proj_qkv",
    "in_proj_z"
  ],
  "in_proj_ba": [
    "in_proj_b",
    "in_proj_a"
  ],

  // Appended to the same mapping by the NPU loader
  "visual": {
    "qkv_proj": [
      "qkv"
    ],
    "gate_up_proj": [
      "gate_proj",
      "up_proj"
    ]
  },
  "vision_model": {
    "qkv_proj": [
      "q_proj",
      "k_proj",
      "v_proj"
    ],
    "proj": [
      "out_proj"
    ]
  },
  "model": {
    "qkv_proj": [
      "q_proj",
      "k_proj",
      "v_proj"
    ],
    "gate_up_proj": [
      "gate_proj",
      "up_proj"
    ],
    "fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa": [
      "q_a_proj",
      "kv_a_proj_with_mqa"
    ],
    "index_qkv_proj": [
      "index_q_proj",
      "index_k_proj"
    ]
  }
}
```

This mapping is used by ModelSlim to resolve an SGLang runtime fused-module name to the corresponding checkpoint-side entry in `quant_model_description.json`. ModelSlim then uses the resolved checkpoint entry to select the quantization scheme, such as W8A8/INT8 or FLOAT.

The mixed mapping is constructed from two sources:

1. The Qwen3.5 model class declares a flat model-specific mapping, including:

   ```python
   "in_proj_qkvz": ["in_proj_qkv", "in_proj_z"],
   "in_proj_ba": ["in_proj_b", "in_proj_a"],
   ```

   Source: [`Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/cebbaacae45ebf669101dde3aac4817ecbb038e0/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L1303-L1311)

2. On NPU, the loader retrieves that model-class mapping and appends the nested `"model"`, `"visual"` and `"vision_model"` mappings.

   Source: [`_get_quantization_config()` NPU mapping injection](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/cebbaacae45ebf669101dde3aac4817ecbb038e0/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py#L218-L251)

The resulting object therefore mixes two different value types:

```text
Dict[str, List[str] | Dict[str, List[str]]]
```

while the original `packed_modules_mapping` contract is a flat:

```text
Dict[str, List[str]]
```

The current ModelSlim implementation selects only one nested subgroup:

```python
key = "model"
if "vision_model" in prefix:
    key = "vision_model"
elif "visual" in prefix:
    key = "visual"

packed_modules_mapping_subset = self.packed_modules_mapping.get(key, {})
```

Source: [`ModelSlimConfig.get_quant_method()`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/cebbaacae45ebf669101dde3aac4817ecbb038e0/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py#L266-L285)

For a language-model layer, this means ModelSlim uses only:

```json
{
  "qkv_proj": [
    "q_proj",
    "k_proj",
    "v_proj"
  ],
  "gate_up_proj": [
    "gate_proj",
    "up_proj"
  ],
  "fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa": [
    "q_a_proj",
    "kv_a_proj_with_mqa"
  ],
  "index_qkv_proj": [
    "index_q_proj",
    "index_k_proj"
  ]
}
```

The model-declared outer mappings for `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba` are still present in the raw object, but become invisible after the `"model"` subgroup is selected.

Consequently, ModelSlim cannot resolve:

```text
in_proj_qkvz -> in_proj_qkv / in_proj_z
in_proj_ba   -> in_proj_b / in_proj_a
```

before querying `quant_model_description.json`. This causes incorrect downstream handling of the W8A8 `in_proj_qkvz` projection and the floating-point `in_proj_ba` projection.

At least three potential fix directions appear possible:

1. Add `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba` to the NPU loader’s hard-coded `"model"` subgroup.
2. Add Qwen3.5 GDN fused-name aliases inside ModelSlim, as proposed in this PR.
3. Teach ModelSlim to understand the existing mixed mapping structure by retaining the model-declared outer flat mappings and applying the selected NPU subgroup as a scoped override.

I am providing this mainly as runtime debug information related to the first bug. The preferred fix likely needs discussion because these alternatives have different compatibility and maintenance trade-offs.

Regarding the second bug described in this PR, **“Vision encoder forced unquantized”**, I noticed a possible compatibility issue in the new prefix-handling logic in `_quant_prefix_candidates()`.

Previously, every candidate that did not start with `language_model.` would also get a `language_model.` version:

```python
if candidate.startswith("language_model."):
    candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("language_model."))
else:
    candidates.append(f"language_model.{candidate}")
```

The PR changes this to:

```python
if candidate.startswith("language_model."):
    candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("language_model."))
elif candidate.startswith("model.visual."):
    candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("model."))
elif candidate.startswith("visual."):
    candidates.append(f"model.{candidate}")
```

The new `model.visual.*` / `visual.*` handling is needed for the quantized vision encoder. However, changing the original `else` into `elif` also means that ordinary candidates no longer get the old `language_model.` fallback.

For example, for this input:

```text
model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
```

the old code generated these candidates:

```text
model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.down_proj
language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
language_model.model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.down_proj
```

With the code in this PR, only these candidates are generated:

```text
model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.down_proj
```

Therefore, these two candidates disappear:

```text
language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj
language_model.model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.down_proj
```

The `language_model.` fallback was added for checkpoints whose quantization metadata keeps that outer prefix, so removing it may affect those checkpoints.

I confirmed the candidate-list difference through static code analysis, but I have not reproduced an actual runtime failure. Would it be safer to keep the language-model prefix handling and the vision prefix handling as two independent operations? For example:

```python
for candidate in list(candidates):
    if candidate.startswith("language_model."):
        candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("language_model."))
    else:
        candidates.append(f"language_model.{candidate}")

    if candidate.startswith("model.visual."):
        candidates.append(candidate.removeprefix("model."))
    elif candidate.startswith("visual."):
        candidates.append(f"model.{candidate}")
```

This keeps the new vision-prefix support while preserving the previous `language_model.` fallback behavior.

### Also required for the `W8A8_MXFP8` path

Confirming this PR is needed beyond the int8 `W8A8_DYNAMIC` case in the issue. We hit the same failure with a ModelSlim **`W8A8_MXFP8`** checkpoint of Qwen3.5-27B on Ascend 950, served through the offline ModelSlim path (`--device npu --tp 1`, scheme auto-detected from `quant_model_description.json`).

**Before this PR**, every GDN layer lost its scheme and then its scales:

```
Unsupported Linear modelslim scheme: [''] in layer: model.language_model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_qkvz
Unsupported Linear modelslim scheme: [''] in layer: model.language_model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_ba
Parameter model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_qkvz.weight_scale not found in params_dict
```

repeated for every linear-attention layer, plus the vision tower (`visual.blocks.*.attn.qkv_proj`, `attn.proj`, `mlp.linear_fc1`, `mlp.linear_fc2`, `visual.merger.*`). The server started and answered, but the output was garbage.

**Why this is not int8-specific.** Three of the four changes here are naming/mapping fixes that run *before* scheme dispatch:

- `loader.py`: `in_proj_qkvz -> [in_proj_qkv, in_proj_z]`, `in_proj_ba -> [in_proj_b, in_proj_a]`
- `modelslim.py::get_quant_method`: redirect to the unfused component name the checkpoint actually stores
- `modelslim.py::_quant_prefix_candidates`: `model.visual.` <-> `visual.`

The lookup fails before `get_linear_scheme()` ever chooses between `ModelSlimW8A8Int8` and `ModelSlimMXFP8Scheme`, so the scheme string in the checkpoint is irrelevant: it returns `None`, the layer becomes `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, and the float8 weights are copied raw into bf16 parameters. Only the fourth change (folding 3-D vision inputs to 2-D in the W8A8 int8 kernels) is int8-specific; `NPUMXFP8LinearMethod` already reshapes to 2-D, so MXFP8 needs nothing there.

**After this PR**: no `Unsupported Linear modelslim scheme` warnings, no `not found in params_dict`, and generation is correct again.

**One caveat for MXFP8, separate from this PR.** Once the vision tower receives the ModelSlim config, `ModelSlimMXFP8Scheme.create_weights` sizes the weight-scale placeholder as `K // 32`, one column short for the vision MLP down projection. A ModelSlim `W8A8_MXFP8` export of Qwen3.5-27B stores it as:

```
model.visual.blocks.0.mlp.linear_fc2.weight        [1152, 4304]   W8A8_MXFP8
model.visual.blocks.0.mlp.linear_fc2.weight_scale  [1152,  135]   W8A8_MXFP8
```

`ceil(4304 / 32) = 135` while the placeholder allocates 134, so the parameter fails to load; 135 is also odd, which the `reshape(n, k // 2, 2)` pair layout in `process_weights_after_loading` cannot consume. Rounding up and padding the odd scale count is in sgl-project/sglang#32745. It is independent of this PR and does not block it -- the same block's `linear_fc1` has `K=1152` with 36 scales and is unaffected.
